Feign
fān
v. (to pretend; rendering Hebrew nakar and shaqar)
From Latin fingere, to shape or invent. To feign is to manufacture an appearance — the same root that gives us fiction.

Biblical Definition

To feign is to pretend. David feigns madness before Achish (1Sa 21:13). Joab sends a wise woman of Tekoah to Absalom's father, telling her to “feign thyself to be a mourner” (2Sa 14:2). Jeroboam's wife is told to feign herself another woman before the blind prophet Ahijah, who names her at the door (1Ki 14:2,5–6). Christ's enemies “sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men” (Luk 20:20), and Jeremiah says Judah returned “feignedly” (Jer 3:10).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines feign as to invent or imagine; to form an idea or conception of something not real; to make a show of, to pretend; to assume a false appearance; and to dissemble.

expand to see more

FEIGN, v.t. To invent or imagine; to form an idea or conception of something not real.

2. To make a show of; to pretend; to assume a false appearance; to counterfeit.

3. To represent falsely; to pretend; to form and relate a fictitious tale.

4. To dissemble; to conceal.

Key Scripture

1Ki 14:5 — "And the LORD said unto Ahijah, Behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh to ask a thing of thee for her son; for he is sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her: for it shall be, when she cometh in, that she shall feign herself to be another woman."

1Ki 14:6 — "And it was so, when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another? for I am sent to thee with heavy tidings."

Luk 20:20 — "And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor."

Jer 3:10 — "And yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah hath not turned unto me with her whole heart, but feignedly, saith the LORD."

Modern Corruption

Pretence is trusted because it usually works, and 1 Kings has a blind prophet greet a disguised queen by name at the door.

expand to see more

1 Kings 14 is a study in the futility of disguise. Jeroboam sends his wife in disguise to a prophet who cannot see, and God tells Ahijah in advance: behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh to ask a thing of thee for her son; for he is sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her: for it shall be, when she cometh in, that she shall feign herself to be another woman. She arrives, and before she speaks he calls out: Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another?

Jeremiah 3:10 applies the word to national repentance, which is the most dangerous place for it: and yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah hath not turned unto me with her whole heart, but feignedly, saith the LORD. A reform had actually happened — Josiah's — with real reforms and real ceremonies. God's assessment was that the turning was performed rather than made, and the exile followed anyway.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew nakar (H5234), to act as a stranger, disguise; shaqar (H8267), falsehood — feignedly is literally in falsehood; Greek hupokrinomai (G5271), to play a part.

expand to see more

Hebrew nakar (H5234) — to disguise, feign; 1 Kings 14:5-6.

Hebrew sheqer (H8267) — falsehood; Jeremiah 3:10, but feignedly.

Greek hupokrinomai (G5271) — to act a part, feign; only Luke 20:20.

Usage

"“Why feignest thou thyself to be another?” — the blind prophet at the door."

"“Which should feign themselves just men” — the spies sent to trap Christ."

"“Not… with her whole heart, but feignedly” — a real reform, performed."
